nodes.label: cold-reviewer agent
nodes.rationale: Read-only reviewer deliberately denied the author's reasoning, so its judgement cannot be contaminated by intent; restricted to Read/Grep/Glob and forbidden from proposing fixes so its output stays pure evidence that converts verbatim into adversarial eval cases.

nodes.label: Silent wrongness (vs. crashes)
nodes.rationale: The deliverable targets wrong output reported as success rather than crashes, because crashes are loud and someone will notice; silent wrongness is the failure class an eval set cannot see.

nodes.label: eval-adversary agent
nodes.rationale: Exists to prove the suite is too easy when it has been green for suspiciously long; maps case coverage to find input-space gaps, and is barred from fixing anything or weakening an invariant to make an input pass.

nodes.label: Real inputs over synthetic corruption
nodes.rationale: Real-world weirdness beats synthetic corruption — an actual odd specimen from the wild exercises variance the pipeline will really meet, whereas hand-mangled files test contrived byte-level tricks.

nodes.label: extraction-auditor agent
nodes.rationale: Audits outputs and the evaluation methodology, never the implementation — it fills the gap left by cold-reviewer (code), eval-adversary (inputs) and spec-drift (docs). Has Bash solely to produce evidence and no write tools by design, so it can fix nothing.

nodes.label: Output audit mode
nodes.rationale: A deliberate reading blindfold: plans, ADR rationale and confidence-derivation docs are forbidden reading so the auditor's sense of a correct boundary comes from the filing itself, not the authors' reasoning.

nodes.label: Confidence miscalibration hunt
nodes.rationale: Hunts high-confidence items that are wrong AND low-confidence items that are right, because miscalibration in either direction is a finding — over-confidence hides errors, under-confidence hides working capability.

nodes.label: Methodology audit mode
nodes.rationale: Checks leakage, gaming, coverage and dual-pass duty; it may read evaluation-strategy and failure-taxonomy docs here because leakage and gaming cannot be detected without knowing what the eval intends to measure.

nodes.label: Held-out leakage check
nodes.rationale: Asks whether a held-out filing's labeled outcome influenced implementation, and whether golden anchors were chosen because the pipeline already passes them — both silently convert a test into a tautology.

nodes.label: Metric gaming check
nodes.rationale: A metric can be satisfied while the extraction is wrong — min_chars set too low, anchors that cannot discriminate, checks a degenerate output passes; so the check is whether a metric is falsifiable at all.

nodes.label: Dual-pass anchor verification
nodes.rationale: A new golden case's anchors are independently re-verified against the raw fixture (grep, count occurrences) before the case is trusted — the author's own verification is not accepted as sufficient.

nodes.label: Standing disagreement is a spec-ambiguity
nodes.rationale: A standing disagreement between auditor and author must be settled by an ADR; a finding is never closed by argument alone, so unresolved judgement calls become durable recorded decisions rather than the loudest voice winning.

nodes.label: spec-drift agent
nodes.rationale: Audits the gap between what the repo SAYS and what it DOES, in four ordered layers (invariants vs cases, contract vs output, ADRs vs code, CLAUDE.md vs reality); read-only, evidence only, severity-ranked.

nodes.label: Decorative invariant
nodes.rationale: An invariant with zero backing invariant-tagged cases is decorative — the worst kind of drift, because it reads as a guarantee while enforcing nothing. Ranked above contract-drift, stale-ADR and stale-doc in severity.

nodes.label: Case authoring SOP
nodes.rationale: Ground truth is anchor-based because offsets cannot be pre-labeled — normalized_text is extractor-owned, so a case that pinned offsets would be labelling the extractor's own output.

nodes.label: Boundary anchors
nodes.rationale: One distinctive phrase from an item's first paragraph and one from its last, chosen normalization-robust (no entities, no tag-spanning text, no page furniture). Occurrence counts are recorded for every anchor: one hit is ideal, exactly 2 is the acceptable TOC pattern, dozens of hits discriminate nothing (audit precedent: 'General Electric', 101 hits).

nodes.label: Deep-tier golden case
nodes.rationale: Full anchor work: fixture provenance, era determination, boundary anchors, grep verification with counts, length bands, cross-item exclusions, watch-it-fail, then dual-pass. The case is not trusted until dual-passed.

nodes.label: Shallow-tier case
nodes.rationale: Steps 1-2 and 7 only, with checks limited to presence/absence, known_items_only, no_overlap_ordered, verbatim, no_empty_success. Minutes per filing — the invariants do the rest, so breadth is bought cheaply.

nodes.label: Held-out case and burn semantics
nodes.rationale: Authored like a deep or shallow case but placed in evals/heldout/ and then deliberately not looked at. Burn semantics: the moment its labeled outcome influences implementation it moves to evals/adversarial/ and is replaced.

nodes.label: Cost discipline
nodes.rationale: Default posture is deterministic code first, LLM last, and never an LLM in a loop you have not bounded — the assignment grades cost/latency judgement explicitly, so the posture is a graded artefact, not an optimisation.

nodes.label: Escalation ladder (regex to big model)
nodes.rationale: regex/parser then heuristic then small model then big model, each stage only seeing what the previous could not handle; per-stage hit-rate is recorded because that number is the evidence in the analysis report.

nodes.label: Content-hash external call cache
nodes.rationale: Key = content hash of input plus prompt/params version, so re-running the eval suite twice costs ~0 the second time; cached responses are committed so the paid `full` suite stays reproducible offline.

nodes.label: Enforced per-run budget
nodes.rationale: A run carries a max-calls / max-tokens counter enforced in code and fails loudly when exceeded — the alternative is silent runaway spend that is only discovered on the invoice.

nodes.label: Eval protocol
nodes.rationale: Defines how to run, read and extend the eval harness — three suites, a case-addition ritual, and baseline discipline; the harness is the spec's execution surface.

nodes.label: invariant suite
nodes.rationale: Properties that must ALWAYS hold; run automatically by the PostToolUse hook after every src/ edit, so it must stay under ~10s or the feedback loop stops being run.

nodes.label: fast suite (pre-commit gate)
nodes.rationale: Golden plus adversarial cases cheap enough to run on every commit (<~60s) with no paid API calls, so the gate can never be skipped for cost or latency reasons.

nodes.label: full suite (slow/paid cases)
nodes.rationale: A tag for slow/expensive cases run before a milestone rather than every commit; `--suite all` exists separately to run everything regardless of tags.

nodes.label: Watch it fail first
nodes.rationale: Write the case, run it, and watch it go red before implementing — an eval that cannot go red is decoration. Where a case passes immediately, the pass must be confirmed legitimate.

nodes.label: Baseline discipline
nodes.rationale: .eval-baseline.json moves only via --update-baseline, deliberately, with an ADR saying why. Downward moves are legitimate (e.g. after adding hard adversarial cases) but must be recorded, so the number can never be quietly bent to make a gate pass.

nodes.label: Read which cases flipped, not the score
nodes.rationale: The gate compares only total score to baseline, so an adversarial FAIL (expected debt) and a golden FAIL (a regression) look identical numerically; the human must eyeball which cases flipped.
nodes.norm_label: read which cases flipped, not the score

nodes.label: Failure triage SOP
nodes.rationale: Never jump from 'it failed' to 'fix it' — the failure class decides where the fix goes and whether the eval set grows, so classification precedes any code change.

nodes.label: Minimal repro becomes the case
nodes.rationale: Shrink the input to the smallest thing that still fails; the minimal repro, not the original blob, becomes the adversarial case so the case tests one thing.

nodes.label: Five failure classes
nodes.rationale: Exactly one of input-variant (fix pipeline), invariant-gap (add the invariant first, watch it fail, then fix), spec-ambiguity (do not code — write an ADR), flake (fix determinism or quarantine, never retry-until-green), eval-bug (fix the eval, note in provenance).

nodes.label: Triage smell checks
nodes.rationale: Fixing the same class in the same module twice means the abstraction is wrong — stop patching and write an ADR. A fix that flips more than two previously-passing cases is reverted and re-triaged.

nodes.label: graphify pipeline
nodes.rationale: Turns any folder of code, docs, papers, images or video into a persistent, queryable knowledge graph with community detection and an honest EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS audit trail; three outputs — interactive HTML, GraphRAG-ready JSON, and a plain-language report.

nodes.label: Structural AST extraction (Part A)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic and free — code needs no LLM and no API key at all, which is why a code-only corpus skips semantic extraction entirely. Run in parallel with the semantic pass since they operate on disjoint file types.

nodes.label: Semantic extraction (Part B subagents)
nodes.rationale: Docs, papers and images are chunked (20-25 files, images alone) and dispatched to parallel general-purpose subagents in one message; Explore subagents are forbidden because read-only agents silently drop results by being unable to write chunk files.

nodes.label: Semantic extraction cache
nodes.rationale: Cache is checked before any subagent is dispatched so only uncached files cost tokens; the cache file is always rewritten or deleted so a stale prior-run cache can never be merged.

nodes.label: Graph shrink guard and empty-graph guard
nodes.rationale: An empty extraction must not clobber a good graph, and a smaller new graph refuses to overwrite the existing graph.json; the report and analysis sidecar are only written when the graph itself was written, so they never describe a graph that graph.json does not contain.
nodes.norm_label: graph shrink guard and empty-graph guard

nodes.label: Graph health check
nodes.rationale: A non-destructive read-only gate surfacing edge collapse, dangling/missing endpoints and self-loops — the silent-corruption modes of incremental updates and AST/LLM id mismatches. Never aborts, but the warning must be surfaced per the Honesty Rules.

nodes.label: Community detection and labeling
nodes.rationale: Clusters are named in 2-5 plain-language words by the host agent, then questions are regenerated because labels affect question phrasing; community detection surfaces cross-document connections nobody would think to ask about.

nodes.label: God nodes and surprising connections
nodes.rationale: High-degree hub nodes and cross-community bridges; the three report sections pasted back to the user are god nodes, surprising connections and suggested questions — the graph is the map, the agent is the guide.

nodes.label: graphify Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge (use AMBIGUOUS when unsure), never skip the corpus warning, always show token cost, never hide cohesion behind symbols, never render >5000 nodes without warning — the audit trail is the product, so a fabricated edge destroys more value than a missing one.

nodes.label: graphify extraction subagent prompt
nodes.rationale: Loaded only when a chunk holds a doc, paper or image; a pure-code corpus never reads it. Passed verbatim so every subagent produces the same schema.

nodes.label: Deterministic node ID format
nodes.rationale: Full repo-relative path with every directory level joined by underscores, so same-named files in different directories stay distinct and the LLM's IDs match the AST extractor's exactly; using only the filename or immediate parent creates orphan ghost-duplicate nodes, and chunk-number suffixes break determinism.

nodes.label: Discrete confidence rubric
nodes.rationale: Five discrete values (0.95/0.85/0.75/0.65/0.55) replace a continuous range because models follow discrete rubrics better — production showed a bimodal collapse (>50% at 0.5, >40% at 0.85+), i.e. the range guidance was being read as a binary.

nodes.label: Verbatim source_file rule
nodes.rationale: Copying the FILE_LIST path character-for-character keeps the full build and incremental --update on the same base, so build_merge's replace-on-re-extract matches the existing node instead of accumulating a duplicate.

nodes.label: Constrained query expansion
nodes.rationale: The query CLI matches by case-folded substring plus IDF with no stemming, synonyms or cross-language matching, so a vocabulary mismatch returns zero hits and collapses the answer to noise. The fix expands the question against the graph's own extracted vocabulary — up to 12 tokens, only tokens actually present, printed to the user so the expansion is auditable, and an empty match is reported rather than faked.

nodes.label: BFS and DFS traversal modes
nodes.rationale: BFS (depth 3) answers 'what is X connected to' with broad nearest-neighbour context; DFS (depth-limited to 6) traces 'how does X reach Y' along one chain. Output is token-budget aware and ranked by relevance before truncation.

nodes.label: Work memory / self-improving loop
nodes.rationale: Answers are saved back with an outcome (useful / dead_end / corrected) so LESSONS.md accumulates preferred sources, known dead ends and prior corrections; reflect --if-stale makes reading them nearly free at session start.

nodes.label: Incremental --update flow
nodes.rationale: Only new/changed files are re-extracted. prune_sources is reserved strictly for genuinely deleted files — changed files are reconciled by build_merge's replace-on-re-extract, and adding changed paths to the prune set would delete the freshly re-extracted content.

nodes.label: Code-only update fast path
nodes.rationale: If every changed file is code, semantic extraction is skipped entirely — no subagents, no LLM, no token cost; only a doc/paper/image/video change forces the full pipeline.

nodes.label: --cluster-only rerun
nodes.rationale: Self-contained: re-clusters, names communities and regenerates report/JSON/HTML from the existing graph. Steps 5-9 must NOT be re-run because a prior build's cleanup deleted the intermediate files they read.

nodes.label: /graphify add URL ingestion
nodes.rationale: Fetches a URL into ./raw with auto-detected handling per type (video to transcript, Twitter via oEmbed, arXiv abstract, PDF, image, webpage to markdown), then runs --update to merge it. Errors are surfaced, never silently continued past.

nodes.label: --watch auto-rebuild
nodes.rationale: Code changes rebuild immediately with no LLM; doc/paper/image changes only raise a needs_update flag. A 3s debounce waits for file activity to stop so a wave of parallel agent writes does not trigger a rebuild per file.

nodes.label: graphify MCP server export
nodes.rationale: A stdio MCP server exposing query_graph, get_node, get_neighbors, get_community, god_nodes, graph_stats and shortest_path so other agents can query the graph live rather than re-deriving it.

nodes.label: Neo4j / FalkorDB Cypher export
nodes.rationale: Uses MERGE so re-running never creates duplicates. For FalkorDB, --push is preferred over the file export because GRAPH.QUERY runs one statement at a time with no bulk script import.

nodes.label: Cross-repo and monorepo graph merge
nodes.rationale: Each repo is built separately then merge-graphs combines them, every node carrying a repo attribute for filtering. For multiple local subfolders the CLI must be used directly because the skill pipeline writes all output to one graphify-out/ in cwd and would clobber itself.

nodes.label: graphify post-commit rebuild hook
nodes.rationale: Triggers once per commit instead of running a background process; detects changed code files via git diff HEAD~1 and re-runs AST extraction only. Appends to an existing post-commit hook rather than replacing it.

nodes.label: Whisper video/audio transcription
nodes.rationale: The host agent composes the Whisper initial prompt itself from god-node labels — it is already a language model, so no separate API call is needed. Transcripts are then treated as ordinary doc files by semantic extraction.

nodes.label: 10-K filing anatomy (sec10k-domain)
nodes.rationale: Domain knowledge loaded on demand: item taxonomy by era, format variants, and ten known extraction traps — each trap is or becomes an adversarial case.

nodes.label: Item taxonomy by era
nodes.rationale: The expected item set is a function of filing year: no 1A/1B/1C or 7A or 9A/9B pre-2003, Item 6 becomes [Reserved] in 2021+, 1C exists from 2023+. An extractor emitting 1A for a 1994 filing has hallucinated (INV-S3).

nodes.label: Format eras (txt / HTML / iXBRL)
nodes.rationale: 1993-2001 plain-text full submissions wrap all documents in <DOCUMENT> blocks with fixed-width page furniture; 2001-2019 is standalone HTML; 2019+ is inline XBRL saturated with <ix:*> tags whose stripping must neither join nor split words.

nodes.label: TOC trap
nodes.rationale: Every item heading appears at least twice (table of contents plus body), so matching the first hit truncates every item at the TOC. AAPL 2025 has exactly 2 hits per heading.

nodes.label: Regulation and cross-reference traps
nodes.rationale: 'Item 405 of Regulation S-K' and 'see Item 8' appear as ordinary prose, so any `Item \d+` regex without a canonical-code filter emits garbage items and in-body cross-references must not open or terminate an item.

nodes.label: Incorporation by reference
nodes.rationale: Part III often contains only a pointer to the proxy statement; that is incorporated_by_reference, not missing and not a tiny 'extracted' item — collapsing the distinction misreports a legitimately absent body as a failure.

nodes.label: Trailing exhibit tail (txt era)
nodes.rationale: GE 1994's 10-K DOCUMENT block continues past SIGNATURES with the full ~280K-char Annual Report inline, so a greedy last-item span swallows it all; the last item must stop at SIGNATURES.

nodes.label: Wild non-canonical item headings
nodes.rationale: Real filings invent item codes — CAT FY2023 contains a literal 'Item 1D' heading with no such Reg S-K item — so canonical-code filtering must reject them; encoded as an any_status absence trap in cat-2023-shallow.

nodes.label: Internal-pointer items
nodes.rationale: JPM 2024 Items 7/8 are ~400-char pointers to pages of the SAME document while the real MD&A and financials sit unlabeled later; the labeled span is extracted and gap validators flag the unlabeled region, since IBR is external-document only (ADR-004).

nodes.label: eval-gate CI workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs the same three commands the pre-commit hook and a human would run. Job names are the contract with branch protection — renaming one silently disables the required check, so they are not cosmetic.

nodes.label: unit-tests job
nodes.rationale: Deliberately runs with no pip install: the pipeline and harness are stdlib-only by decision (ADR-003), so any dependency creeping into this path fails on the import — the cheapest possible enforcement of that decision. Python 3.11 is used because it is the floor declared in pyproject.

nodes.label: invariant-eval job
nodes.rationale: Invariants are absolute: the runner requires 100% with no baseline involved, unlike the score-vs-baseline fast gate.

nodes.label: fast-eval job
nodes.rationale: Compares against .eval-baseline.json — deliberately the same gate as .githooks/pre-commit, so CI and the local hook cannot disagree.

nodes.label: Project working rules (CLAUDE.md)
nodes.rationale: The working contract for the repo. Architecture rationale lives in README.md; CLAUDE.md binds day-to-day behaviour — layout, commands, hard rules, the per-feature loop and the recipe for adding a task.

nodes.label: The eval set IS the spec
nodes.rationale: groundwork targets problems where requirements are clear but correctness is hard to define up front, so correctness is encoded as executable invariants and metrics rather than prose that cannot be run.
nodes.norm_label: the eval set is the spec

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md hard rules
nodes.rationale: Seven binding rules: never hand-edit the baseline, every new failure becomes a watched-red case, specs/ holds only invariants/contracts/ADRs with task state in exactly one ledger, no mocked results (fail loudly instead), commits pass the pre-commit gate, material AI decisions are preserved in prompts/, and commits are consolidated milestones because the evaluators read the history.

nodes.label: Per-feature loop
nodes.rationale: Plan to ADR plus eval cases, watch them fail, implement under the PostToolUse invariant hook, cold-read by cold-reviewer whose findings become adversarial cases, loop back, then commit on green — eval always precedes implementation.

nodes.label: Adding a task recipe
nodes.rationale: Every task needs four artefacts in lockstep: src/<task>/eval_adapter.py exposing run_case, a <task>-domain skill, a specs/0NN-<task>-contract.md, and golden plus adversarial cases tagged with the task name.

nodes.label: Hooks as the only blocking layer
nodes.rationale: .claude/hooks/ and .githooks/ are described as enforcement — the only layer that can actually block. Docs and specs describe and bind on paper; only a hook can stop a bad commit.
nodes.norm_label: hooks as the only blocking layer

nodes.label: AGENTS.md working rules
nodes.rationale: Byte-identical to CLAUDE.md — the same working contract published under the vendor-neutral AGENTS.md filename so non-Claude agents read the same rules.

nodes.label: sec-10k-extract
nodes.rationale: Item-level structured extraction of SEC 10-K filings across three format eras, each item carrying explicit status, character offsets and confidence that does not pretend to be calibrated.

nodes.label: groundwork eval-first scaffold
nodes.rationale: Chosen because 10-K extraction has no public ground truth: correctness must be encoded as executable invariants and hand-labelled cases, and every claim in the README is traceable to a committed report in evals/report/.

nodes.label: Contract-v2 output envelope
nodes.rationale: Item text is readable only through start/end offsets into normalized_text — deliberately no second copy of the text to drift from the offsets (INV-S2).

nodes.label: Four item statuses
nodes.rationale: extracted / incorporated_by_reference / omitted / missing. Every expected item appears with one of the four because silence is never how absence is reported (INV-S4); `missing` is framed as an admission, not a silence.

nodes.label: doc_status and refusal to guess
nodes.rationale: unsupported and failed mean the pipeline refused — it never emits a best-effort parse of a document it could not identify, which is why a 10-Q input yields zero items rather than plausible garbage.

nodes.label: Deterministic first, LLM deferred
nodes.rationale: No model sits in the extraction path, so cost is structurally $0 rather than merely cheap; the LLM fallback stage is deliberately not built until residual-failure data justifies one, and deterministic coverage is currently 100%.

nodes.label: Stdlib-only parsing (ADR-003)
nodes.rationale: html.parser and no dependencies; the revisit clause has never fired because malformed HTML normalizes cleanly. fastapi/uvicorn are needed only by the web inspector.

nodes.label: Offsets, not text
nodes.rationale: Storing offsets instead of a duplicate text copy makes drift structurally impossible rather than something tested against — the whole class of desync bugs cannot occur.

nodes.label: Label-free validator battery
nodes.rationale: Validators needing no annotations run on every filing including ones the eval set has never seen — this is where robustness beyond the labelled fixtures comes from; on held-out filings they caught a real tail bleed unprompted and made a catastrophic under-extraction loud.

nodes.label: Warn, don't hard-fail
nodes.rationale: Validators emit warnings and move confidence; only three may escalate doc_status to ambiguous, so a single suspicious signal degrades the report rather than discarding a usable extraction.

nodes.label: Held-out discipline
nodes.rationale: Five filings authored frozen and structurally unreachable by the normal suites, with results committed before any fix — so the outcome cannot be retro-fitted to the implementation.

nodes.label: Era table is the most brittle component
nodes.rationale: Goldman Sachs FY2002 uses post-SOX numbering ahead of the 2003-08-14 effective date the era table encodes, dropping Item 15 entirely. Found by held-out run H1, predicted in provenance before the run, and deliberately left unfixed because the general repair conflicts with INV-S3.
nodes.norm_label: era table is the most brittle component

nodes.label: Checks structurally incapable of failing
nodes.rationale: Four eval checks cannot fail (verbatim asserts bounds and never compares text) and three validators have never fired on any of the 21 fixtures, so 27/27 green means less than it appears. Recorded rather than papered over: a check nobody can observe is indistinguishable from a check that passed.

nodes.label: Separation of AI roles
nodes.rationale: The valuable part of the AI collaboration was not code generation but role separation: an implementing agent, a cold-reviewer without the author's reasoning, an independent extraction-auditor, and held-out filings that caught what all of them missed. Four separate times a check turned out to be unable to fail.

nodes.label: Measured performance and cost
nodes.rationale: p50/p95 latency 0.041s/0.249s over 21 fixtures, 12.8 MB JPM filing in 0.53s, ~19 MB/s aggregate, 110 MB peak memory, $0.00 per filing — measured rather than estimated, method in docs/analysis-report.md.
